"70% of lottery winners go broke." Where does that number actually come from?

The stat is usually credited to the US National Endowment for Financial Education (NEFE). In January 2018, NEFE said it is not backed by its research and cannot be confirmed: one participant said it at a 2001 NEFE think tank. Meanwhile, a Swedish study (Review of Economic Studies, 2020) surveyed lottery players 5 to 22 years after a win and found big winners' life satisfaction was higher than similar people's, and stayed higher for over a decade. That study measured satisfaction, not bank balances.

What money "fact" have you heard that you'd like us to check?

Sources: NEFE (Jan 12, 2018), Lindqvist, Ostling and Cesarini (2020). Not financial advice.

The popular "70% of lottery winners go broke" stat is usually credited to the National Endowment for Financial Education. In a statement dated Jan 12, 2018, NEFE said it is not backed by its research and cannot be confirmed; a participant said it at a 2001 think tank. A Swedish study (Lindqvist, Ostling and Cesarini, Review of Economic Studies, 2020) surveyed lottery players 5 to 22 years after a win and found large-prize winners' life satisfaction rose and stayed higher for over a decade. It measured satisfaction, not bank balances. Education only, not financial advice. AI narration.
